title: Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One, Background (p. 3)
citation: CISA, Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One: Introduction and Planning, July 2025, section 1.2 Background, page 3: the zero trust shift from implicit trust, allow by default, to explicit verification, deny by default, and the requirement to isolate environments against lateral movement.

title: Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One, Example Scenarios (p. 17)
citation: CISA, Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One: Introduction and Planning, July 2025, section 5 Example Microsegmentation Scenarios, page 17: testing policy in permissive mode with pilot users, segmentation during a cloud transition, and moving branch offices and remote users from VPN to a SASE solution.

title: Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One, Executive Summary (p. 1)
citation: CISA, Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One: Introduction and Planning, July 2025, section 1.1 Executive Summary, page 1: how microsegmentation reduces the attack surface, limits lateral movement and increases visibility, adding to rather than replacing defense in depth.

title: Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One, Key Concepts (p. 9)
citation: CISA, Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One: Introduction and Planning, July 2025, section 2.1 Key Concepts, page 9: microsegments kept small to limit lateral movement, servers allowed to reach only the servers their function needs, segments drawn on application workflows, and boundaries that change as components do.

title: Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One, Segmentation Types (p. 11)
citation: CISA, Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One: Introduction and Planning, July 2025, section 2.2 Segmentation Types, page 11: network, endpoint and container segmentation, including host-based firewalls and agents that enforce segmentation policy on endpoints.

title: Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One, What is Segmentation (p. 5)
citation: CISA, Microsegmentation in Zero Trust, Part One: Introduction and Planning, July 2025, section 2 What is Segmentation, page 5: segments acting as their own networks or subnetworks, enforcement points at segment boundaries that isolate, validate and monitor traffic, and macrosegments such as separated development and production environments and demilitarized zones.

title: OMB M-22-09, Appendix B task matrix (p. 28)
citation: Office of Management and Budget, Memorandum M-22-09, Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles, January 2022, Appendix B Task Matrix, page 28: centralized identity management; phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication; complete asset inventories through the CDM program; endpoint detection and response; authenticated HTTPS for all production HTTP traffic.

title: OMB M-22-09, Appendix B task matrix (p. 29)
citation: Office of Management and Budget, Memorandum M-22-09, Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles, January 2022, Appendix B Task Matrix, page 29: a zero trust architecture plan isolating applications and environments; automated and manual analysis in system authorization; external vulnerability reports for internet-accessible systems; initial categorizations of sensitive documents.
